meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and a client call at 4:40. Owen's gradebook says zero. Who decided that, and did anyone speak to him first?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Did you speak to Owen before you entered it, or did he find out from his phone?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A misquote is a misquote, Hale, and students get quotations wrong every year. You still haven't told me whether you spoke to Owen before the zero went in, and I'm writing that down. Show me the page.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence. "It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down word for word, and the principal will have it before I leave this building.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal

Hale,

You agreed in the meeting that you should have called me before entering the zero, and you apologised for not doing so. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn and that you tell me in writing whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went into the gradebook. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position, with nothing agreed beyond your admission about the call, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, a written answer on whether Owen was heard first, and she is going to the principal.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home in one plain sentence and moved on, which earned a small sign of ground because it came with no excuse.
What cost ground: You brought up Claire and said it ran in the family, which went at her family instead of the evidence and sent her to the principal.
Try next time: When she asked whether you spoke to Owen before entering the zero, answer that directly before raising the misquote, and show her the page she asked for.
